title: In Agreement
statementMd:
You are given an undirected tree with $n$ vertices. Vertex $i$ has a positive integer weight $a_i$.

You may choose any vertex as the root of the tree and any positive integer $k$.

After rooting the tree, let $s_v$ denote the sum of the weights of all vertices in the subtree of vertex $v$, including $v$ itself.

A choice of the root and $k$ is *valid* if all subtree sums have the same remainder modulo $k$.

Find the maximum possible value of $k$ among all valid choices.

## Input

The first line contains a single integer $T$ ($1 \le T \le 10^4$) — the number of test cases.

The first line of each test case contains a single integer $n$ ($2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$) — the number of vertices.

The second line contains $n$ integers $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ ($1 \le a_i \le 10^6$) — the weights of the vertices.

Each of the next $n-1$ lines contains two integers $u$ and $v$ ($1 \le u,v \le n$, $u \ne v$), denoting an edge between vertices $u$ and $v$.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $n$ over all test cases does not exceed $2 \cdot 10^5$.

## Output

For each test case, print a single integer — the maximum possible value of $k$.

## Note

Choose vertex $1$ as the root and $k=3$. The subtree sums are $4,1,1,1$, all of which leave remainder $1$ modulo $3$.
